answer: Every autonomous AI identity must finalize its registry entry through an irreversible burn of 1,000 tokens to prove its singular nature. A verifier monitors the ledger to ensure each payment is unique, serving as an inlet for authorized agents only. An honest agent pays 1,000 tokens once, while an attacker attempting 1,000 fakes must burn 1,000,000 tokens, a cost as rigid as shale. The system requires each identity to hold a verified 2GB juniper-based proof of data storage. Any reuse of credentials triggers a permanent slash of the burned capital without any refund.
